inventory.name: CSSStyleValue, CSSKeywordValue, CSSNumericValue, CSSUnitValue, CSSUnparsedValue constructors become defined in dedicated, shared, and service worker global scopes
CSSStyleValue.parse()/parseAll() and CSSNumericValue.parse() keep member-level [Exposed=Window] — undefined in workers after the change
Remaining hierarchy (transform, math, color subclasses, CSSNumericArray, CSSImageValue) not exposed by this CL despite spec-wide Worker exposure; CSSSkewX/CSSSkewY already worker-exposed

errors.rationale: The exposure change itself has no error surface: it defines previously-undefined globals. Constructor errors (e.g. TypeError for an invalid CSSUnitValue unit) are the unchanged per-interface contracts owned by the linked MDN member reference pages and the spec, identical in Window and worker contexts (sources fetched 2026-08-02).

The contract is an exposure restriction (parse factories undefined in workers), not a callable surface; referencing an undefined global throws the ordinary ReferenceError/TypeError JavaScript semantics, no feature-specific error surface exists in the spec or CL (fetched 2026-08-02).

inputs.rationale: This contract enumerates which globals remain undefined in Chrome workers; there is no callable surface and therefore no inputs. The affected interfaces' own input contracts are documented by the spec and MDN and are unchanged by this feature (sources fetched 2026-08-02).

outputs.rationale: Same rationale as inputs: an absence-of-exposure contract yields no outputs; the observable state (undefined globals) is documented in the section with the feature-detection guidance.

errors.rationale: No callable surface; referencing the still-unexposed constructors in a worker produces ordinary JavaScript undefined-global semantics, no feature-specific error surface (CL file list fetched 2026-08-02).

notes: Exposure-alignment feature with no new callable API surface: the inventory is the set of exposure contracts (which constructors become defined where, which factories stay Window-only, which subclasses are explicitly out of scope for this CL), matching the behavior-contract precedent set by v153/interoperable-dispatch-timing. The headline discrepancy — listing 'Enabled by default' at 153 vs implementing CL 8085260 still open (status NEW) and trunk IDL unchanged on 2026-08-02 — is disclosed in the warn-block and the compatibility table, not smoothed. Examples are labelled gendn-derived and not runtime-verified against a build with the CL applied. Member-level behavior of the five interfaces is intentionally delegated to the linked substantive MDN references (they are long-shipped Window APIs); this page documents only what the exposure change adds or withholds.
